compute.cost_note: stdlib only (tokenization and counting); no spaCy, no API costs

do_not_use_when: you have no writer-specific baseline corpus (--baseline-dir is required)
you want words distinctive to one chapter against the rest of the manuscript (use chapter_distinctiveness_audit)
you want a calibrated AI/human verdict; ratios are revision cues

examples.description: Habit vocabulary across a manuscript against a personal baseline

inputs.target: a manuscript file split by --chapter-pattern, or a --chapter-dir of chapter files

purpose: Manuscript-wide vocabulary repetition. Runs repetition_audit's per-chapter scoring against the writer's external baseline across every chapter, then aggregates into dispersed habit vocabulary (flagged in many chapters), concentrated repetition (one or two chapters at high ratio), and a per-chapter top-N list.
use_when: looking for habit vocabulary that recurs at moderate ratio across many chapters, which a single-chapter audit misses
separating dispersed habits from one-off thematic spikes before a vocabulary restoration pass
